sentences.en: Some of those who have been with Justinian at the palace late at night, men who were pure of spirit thought they saw a strange demoniac form taking his place.
sentences.zh: 据一些深夜在宫中陪伴查士丁尼的人说，那些心灵纯洁的人认为他们看到一个奇怪的恶魔般的形象取代了他的位置。

sentences.en: One man said that the emperor suddenly rose from his throne and walked about, and indeed he was never wont to remain sitting for long.
sentences.zh: 一个人说，皇帝突然从王座上站起来走来走去，事实上他从来不习惯坐太久。

sentences.en: And immediately Justinian's head vanished, while the rest of his body seemed to ebb and flow,
sentences.zh: 紧接着查士丁尼的头部消失了，而他身体的其他部分似乎在起伏不定，

sentences.en: where at the beholder stood aghast and fearful, wondering if his eyes were deceiving him.
sentences.zh: 旁观者看了惊恐万分，甚至怀疑自己的眼睛是不是看错了。

sentences.en: But presently he perceived the vanished head filling out and joining the body again.
sentences.zh: 但随即他发现消失的头部重新充盈并再次连接到身体上。

sentences.en: As strangely as it had left it.
sentences.zh: 就像它离开时一样诡异。

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland, that is the historian Procopius talking of the
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·霍兰，这是历史学家普罗科匹厄斯在谈论

sentences.en: Emperor Justinian, the 6th century emperor of what was then, what they would have called the Roman
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼皇帝，这位六世纪的皇帝统治着当时被他们称为罗马

sentences.en: Empire, what we often call the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 帝国的地方，也就是我们常说的拜占庭帝国。

sentences.en: Do you think Justinian, two questions, do you think he was a demon?
sentences.zh: 你认为查士丁尼——有两个问题——你认为他是一个恶魔吗？

sentences.en: And do you think his head was capable of leaving the body and reappearing on the body afterwards?
sentences.zh: 你认为他的头能够离开身体随后又重新长回身体上吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the two questions are kind of interconnected, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这两个问题有点互相关联，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you could be a demon and not have that power, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你可能是一个恶魔却没有那种超能力。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's unlikely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这不太可能。

sentences.en: I think if you're a demon, you can definitely do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果你是个恶魔，你绝对能做到这一点。

sentences.en: And he goes on to say, doesn't he, that there's another person who comes to Justinian, looks into his face, and the whole of the face melts and becomes a featureless lump of flesh.
sentences.zh: 他接着说，不是吗，还有另一个人来到查士丁尼面前，端详他的脸，结果整张脸都融化了，变成了一团没有任何特征的血肉。

sentences.en: And then gradually the features come back on.
sentences.zh: 然后五官又逐渐恢复了原样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The face changed into a shapeless mass of flesh with neither eyebrows nor eyes in their proper places.
sentences.zh: 这张脸变成了一团没有形状的血肉，眉毛和眼睛都不在它们该有的位置上。

sentences.en: Very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 非常令人不安。

sentences.en: And then what Procopius then goes on to say is that I myself did not witness this, but I spoke to people who definitely saw it, which I don't know.
sentences.zh: 然后普罗科匹厄斯接着说，我自己没有亲眼目睹这一幕，但我跟那些确实亲眼目睹过的人聊过，我不知道该怎么说。

sentences.en: So Justinian, of course, becomes the great lawgiver in Roman history.
sentences.zh: 所以查士丁尼自然成了罗马历史上伟大的立法者。

sentences.en: He compiles this enormous corpus of Roman law, all the kind of the decrees and dictates
sentences.zh: 他汇编了这部庞大的罗马法大全，涵盖了所有来自新罗马

sentences.en: from the new Rome, Constantinople, and from the old Rome, going all the way back to the days of the
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁堡以及旧罗马的法令与指示，一直追溯到共和国

sentences.en: Republic.
sentences.zh: 时期。

sentences.en: And I suspect that Procopius' evidence would not stand up in court when measured against the splendor and gravity of Justinian's own law code.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑普罗科匹厄斯的证词在查士丁尼自己法典的辉煌与庄严面前是经不起法庭检验的。

sentences.en: But we will come to this, won't we, at the end of this episode, because this is part two of an episode on not just Justinian, but also Theodora.
sentences.zh: 但我们会在本集结尾讨论这个，对吧？因为这是关于查士丁尼以及狄奥多拉的一集内容的第二部分。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We talked about how they rise to power in the first episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集里谈到了他们是如何崛起的。

sentences.en: And if you haven't listened to that, you probably should.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没听过那一集，你大概应该去听听。

sentences.en: So we've got to the spring of the year 527.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来到了公元527年的春天。

sentences.en: Justinian, who is from this
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼出身于巴尔干

sentences.en: Balkan background, comes from what is now North Macedonia originally.
sentences.zh: 背景，最初来自现在的北马其顿一带。

sentences.en: His uncle, Justin, had been emperor.
sentences.zh: 他的叔叔查斯丁曾是皇帝。

sentences.en: Justinian has succeeded him.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼继承了他的皇位。

sentences.en: And his wife, Theodora, the circus performer, acrobat, dancer,
sentences.zh: 还有他的妻子狄奥多拉，曾是马戏团艺人、杂技演员、舞者、

sentences.en: prostitute, kind of courtesan, turned empress.
sentences.zh: 妓女、某种交际花，后来成为了皇后。

sentences.en: And she's in her 20s, he's in his 40s, and they have this tremendous project to rebuild the glory of Rome, don't they, Tom?
sentences.zh: 当时她二十多岁，他四十多岁，他们有一个宏大的计划来重振罗马的荣光，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: They absolutely do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此。

sentences.en: So Justinian basically has two mission statements.
sentences.zh: 所以查士丁尼基本上有两个核心使命。

sentences.en: So two goals, one of which is to see the Roman Empire restored to its former dignity.
sentences.zh: 也就是两个目标，其中之一就是让罗马帝国恢复其昔日的尊严。

sentences.en: So by this point, the western half of what had originally been the Roman Empire has gone.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，原本的罗马帝国的西半部分已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: So Britain, obviously, Gaul, Spain,
sentences.zh: 所以显然不列颠、高卢、西班牙、

sentences.en: Italy, North Africa, and Justinian dreams of getting them back.
sentences.zh: 意大利、北非都丢了，而查士丁尼梦想着把它们夺回来。

sentences.en: But the other thing that he dreams of is seeing heaven established on earth.
sentences.zh: 但他的另一个梦想是在人间建立天堂。

sentences.en: He's a very, very devout Christian.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常非常虔诚的基督徒。

sentences.en: And essentially, the two ambitions are not entirely disconnected.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这两个抱负并不是完全脱节的。

sentences.en: Because he sees the power and the splendor and the might of the Roman Empire as being expressive of God's plans for the whole of humanity.
sentences.zh: 因为他将罗马帝国的权势、辉煌和强大视为上帝对全人类计划的表达。

sentences.en: So if he can win God's favor, if he can reorder the Roman Empire to reflect the will of God, then God's favor will descend on the empire.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他能赢得上帝的青睐，如果他能重新整顿罗马帝国以反映上帝的意志，那么上帝的恩典就会降临到帝国身上。

sentences.en: And hopefully, before you know it, the legions will be back in Britain.
sentences.zh: 说不定转眼之间，军团就重返不列颠了。

sentences.en: And it's another thing that binds them, Tom, his belief in the dignity and the importance of the office of emperor, and of central control and central power.
sentences.zh: 这也是将他们联系在一起的另一件事，汤姆，那就是他对皇帝职位以及中央控制和中央权力的尊严和重要性的坚定信仰。

sentences.en: Because obviously, one of the things that what had happened to the Roman world, generally, I suppose you would say in the previous
sentences.zh: 因为显然，罗马世界在过去

sentences.en: 200 years or so, was a kind of this sort of centrifugal process where bits were breaking off,
sentences.zh: 两百年左右的时间里普遍发生的一件事，可以说是某种离心过程，各部分纷纷分裂，

sentences.en: where authority was being challenged and authority passing to local warlords and things who end up
sentences.zh: 权威受到挑战，权力转交给地方军阀之类的人，最终在长期来看，他们成了各个王国的国王。

sentences.en: becoming, in the long run, kings of kingdoMs. And a lot of Justinian's projects, seems to me,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，查士丁尼的许多项目，

sentences.en: is about reasserting Constantinople's control, whether it be in religion, or indeed, you talked
sentences.zh: 都关乎重申君士坦丁堡的控制权，无论是宗教方面的，还是你刚才提到的法律——改革法律，亦或是对意大利和北非等地的实际控制。

sentences.en: about law, reforming the laws, or physical control over Italy and North Africa and so on.
sentences.zh: 难道你不认为这占了很大一部分吗？

sentences.en: And don't you think that's a lot of it?
sentences.zh: 所以当他想到你所说的人间天堂时，那就是上帝或基督的统治，对吧？

sentences.en: So that when he thinks about heaven on earth, as you put it, that's the rule of God or Christ, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 单一神祇的统治。

sentences.en: The rule of the one deity.
sentences.zh: 一个皇帝的统治和一个神的统治这种理念，我的意思是，对她或他来说基本上是一回事，对吧？

sentences.en: And the idea of the rule of one emperor and the rule of one God, I mean, they're kind of the same thing to him, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 好吧，不过当然了，皇帝并不控制教会。

sentences.en: Well, except that, of course, the emperor does not control the church.
sentences.zh: 但他很乐意掌控。

sentences.en: But he likes it.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁堡牧首显然比罗马主教，甚至亚历山大港的牧首或教宗，更加听命于他。

sentences.en: The patriarch of Constantinople is much more under his thumb, obviously, than the Bishop of Rome is, say, or even the patriarch of the Pope in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 但即使是君士坦丁堡牧首，其对上帝的责任也与皇帝有着不同的层级。

sentences.en: But even the patriarch in Constantinople is a figure whose responsibility to God is of a different order to the emperors.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得

sentences.en: So I think that
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼绝对把自己看作是上帝任命的教会之盾和捍卫者。

sentences.en: Justinian does absolutely see himself appointed by God to serve as the shield and defender of the church.
sentences.zh: 他无疑认为自己被安置在那里，被安置在人世间是为了给教会带来统一。

sentences.en: And he undoubtedly sees himself as set there, set on earth to bring unity to the church.
sentences.zh: 而且查士丁尼对自己的神学家身份感到非常非常自豪。

sentences.en: And Justinian is very, very proud of himself as a kind of theologian.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢把教会人士找来，然后训斥和教导他们。

sentences.en: He likes to get churchmen in and then berate them and kind of lecture them.
sentences.zh: 他绝对认为铲除异端是自己的职责所在。

sentences.en: And he definitely, you know, he sees it as his duty to stamp out heresy.
sentences.zh: 他认为尽一切努力关闭异教哲学最后的据点是自己的天职。

sentences.en: He sees it as his duty to do all that he can to close down kind of the remaining strongholds of pagan philosophy.
sentences.zh: 因此，查士丁尼作为据称关闭了雅典柏拉图学派的人物而声名狼藉。

sentences.en: So Justinian is notorious as the figure who closes down supposedly the Platonic school in Athens.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，真相大相径庭。

sentences.en: Which, in fact, the truth is rather different.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是什么

sentences.en: This isn't the
sentences.zh: 柏拉图学派。

sentences.en: Platonic school.
sentences.zh: 柏拉图学派早在很久很久以前的公元前一世纪就被摧毁了。

sentences.en: The Platonic school had been destroyed long, long before back in the first century BC.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个在公元四世纪建立的学派。

sentences.en: So, but this is a school that had been set up in the fourth century.
sentences.zh: 它并不是真正的

sentences.en: It's not really
sentences.zh: 柏拉图主义。

sentences.en: Platonic.
sentences.zh: 它是新柏拉图主义。

sentences.en: It's neoplatonic.
sentences.zh: 它非常神秘主义。

sentences.en: It's very mystic.
sentences.zh: 有点古怪。

sentences.en: It's kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 里面全都是——你知道的，这根本不是什么希腊理性主义的据点之类的地方。

sentences.en: It's full of, you know, this is not a kind of stronghold of Greek rationalism or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 而查士丁尼所做的，其实并不是禁掉它，而是停止了中央资助，即来自政府的资金支持。

sentences.en: And what Justinian does, he doesn't actually ban it, but he stops kind of central funding, funding from the government.
sentences.zh: 哲学学派确实还在其他地方存续，比如在亚历山大港以及类似的地方。

sentences.en: And philosophical schools do remain in, well, in Alexandria, for instance, places like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种传统还在勉强维持，但这种哲学传统的丧钟已经敲响了。

sentences.en: So, so that kind of ticks along, but the, the, the writing is on the wall for, for that kind of philosophical tradition.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他在铲除异端方面非常非常残酷。

sentences.en: And as I say, he's, he's very, very brutal in stamping at heresy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他有着对连贯性和秩序的执念。

sentences.en: So there's an obsession with coherence and order.
sentences.zh: 绝对的连贯性。

sentences.en: Absolute coherence.
sentences.zh: 他认为做到这一点是自己的责任。

sentences.en: And he sees it as his duty to do this.
sentences.zh: 而其中一种体现方式就是，存在着某种日历。

sentences.en: And one, one of the kind of the, the measures of this is that there's, there's a kind of calendar.
sentences.zh: 而这个日历的装饰品之一就是挂在长矛上的异端分子的头颅。

sentences.en: And one of the ornaments for this calendar is the heads of heretics on Sykes.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 这有点像基督降临日历之类的东西。

sentences.en: Which is kind of like an advent calendar or something.
sentences.zh: 那是你在中餐馆之类的地方能拿到那种日历吗？

sentences.en: Is that a calendar you get from a Chinese restaurant or something?
sentences.zh: 差不多的东西。

sentences.en: Kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他认为这是他职责的一部分，但当然了，正如我们在第一部分中提到的，

sentences.en: I mean, he sees that as part of his duty, but, but also of course, you know, we mentioned in, in the first part that there's this kind of division within the
sentences.zh: 帝国内部存在着这样一种分裂：一方面是作为正统基督徒的迦克墩派，另一方面是主要集中在亚历山大港、埃及以及黎凡特其他地区的基督一性论派。

sentences.en: emperor between the Chalcedonians who are the Orthodox Christians and Monophysites who are centered much more in, in Alexandria and Egypt and other parts of the, the, the Levant.
sentences.zh: 而狄奥多拉当然是个基督一性论者。

sentences.en: And of course, Theodora is a Monophysite.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我认为他们的关系是——

sentences.en: So there's a sense in which I think that their relationship is, you know, he's, he is saying,
sentences.zh: 他通过极度珍视狄奥多拉、极力提拔她，其实是在向基督一性论派表态：

sentences.en: you know, by, he's saying, you know, by, by treasuring Theodora so much, by promoting her so high, he is kind of saying to the Monophysites, you know, we, you are still Christian.
sentences.zh: 你们依然是基督徒。

sentences.en: Um, you know, you are still kind of beloved as I, as I love Theodora.
sentences.zh: “你们依然像我深爱狄奥多拉那样被我所爱戴。”

sentences.en: So that's a part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是其中一部分。

sentences.en: But in the other areas that you mentioned, so law particularly and military conquest, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但在你提到的其他领域，尤其是法律和军事征服方面，绝对如此。

sentences.en: Justinian sees himself as appointed by God.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼视自己为受命于天。

sentences.en: There's one other element I want to ask your opinion about.
sentences.zh: 我还想就另一个元素征求一下你的意见。

sentences.en: So, um, we talked in the first episode about Rome's great rival.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们第一集里谈到了罗马的劲敌。

sentences.en: I mean, by far Rome's biggest rival, which is Persia.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，罗马最大的竞争对手莫过于波斯。

sentences.en: So throughout the sixth century, Rome is facing a different kind of Persian empire than the one that it had faced a few generations, a couple of generations earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以在整个六世纪，罗马面对的波斯帝国，与它几个世纪前、也就是几代人之前面对的波斯帝国有所不同。

sentences.en: So a much more self-confident, much more coherent, um, Sasanian, it's the Sasanian dynasty that are running the
sentences.zh: 这是一个自信得多、内部更加连贯的萨珊王朝，正是萨珊王朝在统治着

sentences.en: Persian empire.
sentences.zh: 波斯帝国。

sentences.en: And at the same time that Justinian's reign is almost exactly kind of coincidental with that of a guy called Khosrow in Persia, who is himself a centralizer, a massive reformer,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，查士丁尼的统治几乎与波斯一个名叫霍斯劳的人的统治完全重合，霍斯劳本人也是一个集权主义者、大改革家，

sentences.en: really beefing up the, the power of the kind of Persian monarchy and the Persian state.
sentences.zh: 真正极大地增强了波斯君主制和波斯国家的实力。

sentences.en: And there are some historians on there who say, well, what Justinian is doing is basically an
sentences.zh: 有些历史学家认为，查士丁尼所做的一切基本上是

sentences.en: attempt to kind of tool up the Roman empire so that it can properly compete with its big Persian rival.
sentences.zh: 试图武装罗马帝国，好让它能够与波斯这个强大的对手好好竞争。

sentences.en: How much do you think that's true, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你觉得这有多大程度是真实的？

sentences.en: You're right that Khosrow is the great rival of Justinian and might all make, might even have been
sentences.zh: 你说得对，霍斯劳是查士丁尼的劲敌，甚至可能

sentences.en: his brother because, um, Khosrow's father, Kaved, a very formidable figure, had kind of repaired the
sentences.zh: 是他的兄弟，因为霍斯劳的父亲卡瓦德是一个非常了不起的人物，在波斯帝国被匈人入侵摧毁后，他修复了波斯帝国，真正让它重组了起来，但随后却接受了某种激进形式的琐罗亚斯德教。

sentences.en: Persian empire after it had been shattered by a Hunnic invasion, really put it back together, but had then signed up to a kind of radical form of Zoroastrianism.
sentences.zh: 琐罗亚斯德教是伊朗、波斯的国教。

sentences.en: Zoroastrianism is the, the state religion of, of Iran, of Persia.

sentences.zh: 时间是公元532年1月10日。

sentences.en: We are in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我们在君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: In the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 在竞技场里。

sentences.en: The stands are packed.
sentences.zh: 看台上挤满了人。

sentences.en: Everybody is looking forward to a great day of sport.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在期待一场精彩的体育盛事。

sentences.en: Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Great day of sport and a great day of rioting.
sentences.zh: 精彩的体育盛事，还有精彩的暴乱。

sentences.en: Because, of course, for the rival factions, the Blues and the Greens,
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，对于蓝党和绿党这两个敌对派别来说，

sentences.zh: 打一架的机会是娱乐中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And the Blues and the Greens all start piling into each other.
sentences.zh: 于是蓝党和绿党开始互相群殴。

sentences.en: There's a riot.
sentences.zh: 发生暴动了。

sentences.en: Various bits of infrastructure outside the Hippodrome catch fire.
sentences.zh: 竞技场外面的各种基础设施着火了。

sentences.en: Justinian sends the troops in to crack heads and restore law and order.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼派军队进去镇压并恢复法律与秩序。

sentences.en: The ringleaders get arrested.
sentences.zh: 领头闹事的人被捕了。

sentences.en: And these ringleaders are both Blues and Greens.
sentences.zh: 这些领头人既有蓝党，也有绿党。

sentences.en: And the following day, they are hanged.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他们被绞死了。

sentences.en: I think there are eight of them.
sentences.zh: 我想他们大概有八个人。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think there's about eight of them, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有八个人吧，对。

sentences.en: So there are about eight of them.
sentences.zh: 所以大概有八个人。

sentences.en: And six of them all goes well.
sentences.zh: 其中六个人一切顺利。

sentences.en: They all die.
sentences.zh: 他们都死了。

sentences.en: Well, not well for them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对他们来说可不太顺利。

sentences.en: Yeah, but for Justinian.
sentences.zh: 对，但对查士丁尼来说很顺利。

sentences.en: And you're very much on the side of Justinian.
sentences.zh: 而你非常支持查士丁尼。

sentences.en: I am indeed, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的确很支持，是的。

sentences.en: He did it and he was right to do it.
sentences.zh: 他做了这件事，而且他做得对。

sentences.en: But two of them, the rope snaps.
sentences.zh: 但有两个人，绳子断了。

sentences.en: And one of these lucky people is a Blue.
sentences.zh: 其中一个幸运儿是蓝党。

sentences.en: And one of them is a Green.
sentences.zh: 另一个是绿党。

sentences.en: And they kind of get bundled up by monks, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们被修道士们裹挟着带走了，对吧？

sentences.en: And taken across the Bosphorus to a monastery on the other side or a church.
sentences.zh: 被带过博斯普鲁斯海峡，去到对岸的一个修道院或教堂。

sentences.en: And there they're able to claim sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 在那里他们得以寻求避难。

sentences.en: And so then there's a kind of issue of what happens.
sentences.zh: 接下来就产生了一个问题：接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: What's going to happen next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会怎么样？

sentences.en: And pressure grows on Justinian to issue a pardon.
sentences.zh: 要求查士丁尼颁布特赦令的压力越来越大。

sentences.en: And on the 14th of January, Justinian comes to the Hippodrome, takes his seat and announces that he's not going to pardon them.
sentences.zh: 1月14日，查士丁尼来到竞技场，就座并宣布他不会特赦他们。

sentences.en: And Dominic, what is the result of that?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，结果怎么样？

sentences.en: Does this go down well?
sentences.zh: 这事能顺利过去吗？

sentences.en: The crowd goes absolutely mental, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 人群彻底疯狂了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, people just start roaring and shouting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们开始怒吼和呐喊。

sentences.en: And clearly, there's been some orchestration, I would say.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这是经过精心策划的，我觉得。

sentences.en: And we were talking before the break about the sort of disquiet of people who don't like Justinian's new taxes.
sentences.zh: 我们在中场休息前谈过那些对查士丁尼的新税收感到不满的人的焦虑情绪。

sentences.en: They probably don't like the fact that he is expecting greater public obedience and self-abnegation to him and to Theodora.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不喜欢他期望公众对他和狄奥多拉表现出更大的服从和自我牺牲。

sentences.en: There are probably lots of people, actually, who regard them as parvenues, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 实际上，可能很多人认为他们是暴发户，对吧？

sentences.en: Who think, oh, he's just some bullpen peasant and she's an ex-prostitute.
sentences.zh: 心想：哦，他不过是个军营里的乡巴佬，而她是个前妓女。

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在干什么？

sentences.en: Among the Senate, definitely.
sentences.zh: 在元老院中，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: These ghastly people.
sentences.zh: 这些讨厌的家伙。

sentences.en: So there's probably an element of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中可能包含这种因素。

sentences.en: And there's also clearly an element of the crowd being, you know, tanked up and enjoying a punch up and stuff.
sentences.zh: 显然也有一种因素，就是群众被灌了酒，正享受着打群架之类的乐趣。

sentences.en: And so the crowd start chanting at him as they go berserk.
sentences.zh: 于是，当人群陷入狂乱时，开始向他高声叫骂。

sentences.en: And they start chanting as one, famously, Nika, Nika, or Nika, Nika, depending on your pronunciation, which basically means victory, victory, or conquer, conquer, which is,
sentences.zh: 他们异口同声地高喊着著名的口号：“尼卡，尼卡”（Nika, Nika），取决于你的发音，这基本上意味着“胜利，胜利”或“征服，征服”，也就是，

sentences.en: I guess, which is what they would have chanted anyway.
sentences.zh: 我想，反正这也是他们平时会喊的。

sentences.en: Am I right, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: During the races.
sentences.zh: 在比赛期间。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But also, you know, the one that wins, then they do the chanting.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，赢的那一方，他们就会这样喊。

sentences.en: And so half the crowd will chant it and half won't.
sentences.zh: 所以一半的观众会喊，另一半不会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because, you know, half has backed the side that's won, half has backed the side that's loSt.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，一半人支持了赢的一方，一半人支持了输的一方。

sentences.en: The thing that is unbelievably ominous and must have been completely terrifying for Justinian is that now the whole Hippodrome is chanting this.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的不祥预兆、对查士丁尼来说绝对堪称恐怖的是，现在整个竞技场都在高喊这个口号。

sentences.en: And they're doing it as unison.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是异口同声地喊。

sentences.en: And it becomes obvious to him that the greens and the blues have teamed up.
sentences.zh: 他终于明白，绿党和蓝党联手了。

sentences.en: And they all spill out of the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 他们全都涌出竞技场。

sentences.en: And basically, they start disassembling the center of Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们开始拆毁君士坦丁堡的市中心。

sentences.en: Yeah, burning, pillaging.
sentences.zh: 对，纵火，劫掠。

sentences.en: And so we mentioned, so Hagia Sophia, the great cathedral of Constantinople, goes up in flames.
sentences.zh: 正如我们提到的，圣索菲亚大教堂——君士坦丁堡伟大的大教堂，付之一炬。

sentences.en: The Augusteion, which is the kind of the great open space next to Hagia Sophia, and the Schalke, the bronze gates that lead into the palace, that goes up in flames.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯提翁广场（圣索菲亚大教堂旁巨大的开阔地），以及通往皇宫的青铜大门查克（Schalke），都付之一炬。

sentences.en: The baths of Zyxippus go up in flames.
sentences.zh: 宙克西帕斯浴场付之一炬。

sentences.en: So that's the baths that had all the classical statuary.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个藏有所有古典雕塑的浴场。

sentences.en: So it's a bit like the British Museum going up in flames.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像大英博物馆付之一炬。

sentences.en: I mean, everything just gets loSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一切都化为乌有。

sentences.en: And basically, it's absolute carnage.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一场绝对的大屠杀。

sentences.en: And Justinian tries to kind of reimpose order.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼试图恢复秩序。

sentences.en: So he sends in, I think, about 1,500 troops.
sentences.zh: 所以他派出了我想大约1500名军队。

sentences.en: And they're able to kind of stabilize the situation so that the palace itself is not under threat.
sentences.zh: 他们能够稳定局势，使皇宫本身免受威胁。

sentences.en: But they can't bring central Constantinople back under order.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法让君士坦丁堡市中心恢复秩序。

sentences.en: And it just gets worse and worse and worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 而且情况变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's five days.
sentences.zh: 对，持续了五天。

sentences.en: Five days before he goes back to the Hippodrome to address the crowd.
sentences.zh: 过了五天他才回到竞技场向人群讲话。

sentences.en: And at this point, he's been reduced, basically, to begging.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，他基本上已经沦落到乞求的地步。

sentences.en: So he says, you know, if you please go home, I'll give you an amnesty.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，求求你们回家吧，我给你们大赦。

sentences.en: You know, there'll be a free pardon.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，会有无条件特赦。

sentences.en: And they howl him down at this point.
sentences.zh: 而此时群众发出了嘘声把他的声音压了下去。

sentences.en: And at this point, Tom, now you mentioned, and I think in the previous episode, that there was somebody else who could have been emperor, who was called Hypatious,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你之前和上一集中提到的，当时还有另一个人可以当皇帝，名叫希帕蒂乌斯（Hypatious），

sentences.en: who had been a commander away on the frontiers.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名远在边境的指挥官。

sentences.en: And the nephew of Anastasius.
sentences.zh: 还是阿纳斯塔西乌斯的侄子。

sentences.en: And he's quite old.
sentences.zh: 他年纪挺大了。

sentences.en: But at this point, he reemerges as a significant figure because some of the crowds say, he's the man we want as emperor.
sentences.zh: 但此时他又作为一个重要人物重新出现，因为一些群众说：他才是我们想要的皇帝。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not unprecedented, right, for crowds to go berserk and to call for new emperors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，群众狂乱并呼唤新皇帝，这并非史无前例，对吧？

sentences.en: And, you know, if you lose the support of the army and of the palace guard, then you're toast, basically.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你失去了军队和宫廷卫队的支持，那你就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: That must be the fear that Justinian has at this point.
sentences.zh: 这一定就是查士丁尼此刻的恐惧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, Hypatious doesn't, I think, want to be emperor at all.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，希帕蒂乌斯其实一点也不想当皇帝。

sentences.en: You know, he really doesn't, particularly because he knows that if Justinian succeeds in restabilizing everything, then he's absolute toaSt.
sentences.zh: 他真的不想，特别是他知道如果查士丁尼成功恢复了秩序，那他就死定了。

sentences.en: But it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 但这没关系。

sentences.en: The crowds pick him up.
sentences.zh: 群众拥立了他。

sentences.en: They hail him as emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们高呼他为皇帝。

sentences.en: And the destruction continues.
sentences.zh: 破坏仍在继续。

sentences.en: And Justinian is very anxious by this point, whether he can trust anyone, whether he can trust his soldiers, whether he can trust his officials.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼此时非常焦虑，不知道自己还能信任谁，能否信任他的士兵，能否信任他的官员。

sentences.en: And he starts to contemplate flight.
sentences.zh: 他开始考虑逃跑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he orders ships to be prepared.
sentences.zh: 于是他命令准备船只。

sentences.en: So, you know, because there are harbors in the palace, so he could escape from that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为皇宫里有港口，所以他可以从那里逃走。

sentences.en: And it is at this point that Theodora shows her mettle.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，狄奥多拉展现了她的风骨。

sentences.en: Probably the most famous contribution to history, apart from that business with the geese, Tom.
sentences.zh: 除了关于大鹅的那段插曲之外，这大概是她对历史最著名的贡献了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Would you like me to read Theodora's, what Theodora says?
sentences.zh: 你想让我读一下狄奥多拉的话吗？

sentences.en: I would love you to, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意你读一下。

sentences.en: She says, every man who is born into the light of day must sooner or later die.
sentences.zh: 她说：凡是降生于世的人，迟早都免不了一死。

sentences.en: And how could an emperor ever allow himself to be a fugitive?
sentences.zh: 皇帝又怎么能容许自己成为一个逃亡者呢？

sentences.en: May I myself never willingly shed my imperial robes, nor see the day when I am no longer addressed by my title.
sentences.zh: 愿我永远不会被迫脱下这身皇袍，也永远不要看到我不再被称为陛下的那一天。

sentences.en: If you, my lord, wish to save your skin, well, you will have no difficulty in doing so.
sentences.zh: 陛下，如果你想保全性命，那轻而易举。

sentences.en: We are rich.
sentences.zh: 我们很富有。

sentences.en: There is the sea.
sentences.zh: 外面有大海。

sentences.en: There are our ships.
sentences.zh: 那里有我们的船只。

sentences.en: But consider first whether when you reach safety, you will not regret that you did not choose death in preference.
sentences.zh: 但请先想一想，当你到达安全地带时，你是否会后悔自己没有选择死亡？

sentences.en: As for me, I stand by the ancient saying, the purple is the noblest winding sheet.
sentences.zh: 至于我，我坚守那句古老的格言：紫袍是最尊贵的裹尸布。

sentences.en: Iron lady.
sentences.zh: 铁娘子。

sentences.en: Is that how you imagine Theodora speaking, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是你想象中狄奥多拉说话的样子吗？

sentences.en: But to a degree, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，在某种程度上是的。

sentences.en: So Theodora is very keen to crush the enemy within.
sentences.zh: 所以狄奥多拉非常热衷于消灭内部的敌人。

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 她确实如此。

sentences.en: She's facing rioters.
sentences.zh: 她面对的是暴徒。

sentences.en: She's facing strikers.
sentences.zh: 她面对的是罢工者。

sentences.en: And so what are you going to do in that situation?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下你该怎么做？

sentences.en: You're going to recruit new platoons of police, which is basically what Justinian is shamed by this kind of iron resolve.
sentences.zh: 你要招募新的警察队伍，而查士丁尼正是被这种钢铁般的决心所激励，

sentences.en: And a whole load of troops conveniently do turn up.
sentences.zh: 一大批军队也恰好赶到了。

sentences.en: One is under the command of a barbarian from the Danube called Amundus.
sentences.zh: 其中一支由来自多瑙河的蛮族将领阿蒙达斯（Amundus）指挥。

sentences.en: So he has a load of craft troops.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一支精锐部队。

sentences.en: Fortunately, they're available in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他们当时正好在君士丁堡。

sentences.en: And the other is under the command of a very famous figure, probably Justinian's most famous general, the hero of a novel by Robert Graves, Belisarius.
sentences.zh: 另一支由一位非常著名的人物指挥，大概是查士丁尼最著名的将军、罗伯特·格雷夫斯小说中的英雄——贝利撒留。

sentences.en: And these troops get kind of, you know, rather like Mrs. Thatcher getting the police, getting the Met to go and break the strike in Nottingham.
sentences.zh: 这些军队就像撒切尔夫人派警察去诺丁汉镇压罢工那样，

sentences.en: Justinian and Theodora mass these troops and send them into the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼和狄奥多拉集结了这些军队，把他们派进了竞技场。

sentences.en: And by this point, Justinian has kind of reactivated his link with the Blues and has said, you know, watch out, guys.
sentences.zh: 此时，查士丁尼恢复了与蓝党的联系，并传话道：小心点，伙计们。

sentences.en: You don't want to die to defend the Greens.
sentences.zh: 你们可不想为保护绿党而死。

sentences.en: So most of the Blues by this point, if not all, but most have left the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 所以在此时，大部分甚至全部蓝党都离开了竞技场。

sentences.en: So you've got the Greens, you've got a few stragglers.
sentences.zh: 所以里面只剩下绿党和一些零星的滞留者。

sentences.en: They're all unarmed.
sentences.zh: 他们都没有武装。

sentences.en: They're in the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 他们都在竞技场里。

sentences.en: And Mundus' troops come in one end.
sentences.zh: 阿蒙达斯的军队从一头冲进去。

sentences.en: Belisarius has come in the other.
sentences.zh: 贝利撒留从另一头冲进去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they just kind of cut their way through and they slaughter everybody in their path.
sentences.zh: 他们一路杀过去，屠杀了路上遇到的所有人。

sentences.en: And actually, one person you haven't mentioned, Tom, for those who get out, there are more troops waiting outside under the command of somebody called Narcisse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，还有一个你没提到的人，汤姆，对于那些逃出去的人，外面还有更多军队在纳尔西斯（Narcisse）的指挥下等待着。

sentences.en: Oh, I forgot Narcisse.
sentences.zh: 哦，我把纳尔西斯给忘了。

sentences.en: How could you forget Narcisse, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能忘掉纳尔西斯呢，汤姆？

sentences.en: He was one of the eunuchs, wasn't he, in our 10 top eunuchs.
sentences.zh: 他可是我们十大太监之一，对吧？

sentences.en: So newcomers to the podcast will be delighted to hear we have an episode about the top 10 eunuchs in history.
sentences.zh: 所以播客的新听众会很高兴听到我们有一集关于历史上十大太监的节目。

sentences.en: And Narcisse is probably the top Armenian eunuch in history.
sentences.zh: 而纳尔西斯可能是历史上最厉害的亚美尼亚太监。

sentences.en: He's of Armenian descent.
sentences.zh: 他是亚美尼亚血统。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's about, I mean, we talked about, we compared Justin with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 他大概是，我是说，我们聊过，我们把查士丁与乔·拜登作了对比。

sentences.en: I mean, I think Narcisse makes Joe Biden look positively youthful because Narcisse is about 140, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得纳西索斯让乔·拜登显得格外年轻，因为纳西索斯大概有140岁了，对吧？

sentences.en: But he's a tremendous, I mean, he's an immensely impressive man.
sentences.zh: 但他非常了不起，我是说，他是一个极其令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: And very loyal to Justinian.
sentences.zh: 而且对查士丁尼非常忠诚。

sentences.en: And if you listened in the first part, you may remember that Justin at this point, Justinian's predecessor, uncle,
sentences.zh: 如果你听了第一部分，你可能还记得查士丁在这个时候，也就是查士丁尼的前任、叔叔，

sentences.en: he becomes emperor because he gets given large amounts of gold to go out and bribe people to support one of the pretenders.
sentences.zh: 他之所以成为皇帝，是因为他得到了大量的黄金，出去收买人们去支持其中一个觊觎皇位者。

sentences.en: And Justin just pockets the gold.
sentences.zh: 而查士丁把黄金全揣进了自己腰包。

sentences.en: So Narcisse is given gold by Justinian to go and do the same.
sentences.zh: 所以查士丁尼给了纳西索斯黄金，让他去效仿。

sentences.en: But Narcisse, unlike Justin, stays loyal and true.
sentences.zh: 但纳西索斯与查士丁不同，他始终忠诚而坚定。

sentences.en: And he goes out and he bribes all the various ringleaders.
sentences.zh: 他走了出去，收买各派的头目。

sentences.en: He bribes the various senators to calm down.
sentences.zh: 他收买各位参议员让他们冷静下来。

sentences.en: And this is what kind of precedes the ability of Belisarius and Mundus to slaughter everyone in the Hippodrome.
sentences.zh: 而这正是贝利撒留和蒙都斯得以在竞技场屠杀所有人的前奏。

sentences.en: That's not a bad choice for Narcisse.
sentences.zh: 这对纳西索斯来说是个不错的选择。

sentences.en: I mean, Narcisse has a tremendous life, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纳西索斯过着极了不起的生活，对吧？

sentences.en: He does, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he has a great career, as we shall see.
sentences.zh: 我是说，正如我们接下来所看到的，他有着辉煌的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Well, I'm under St. Belisarius, Steve.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是圣贝利撒留的手下，史蒂夫。

sentences.en: They all do, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们都是如此，是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they've killed all the other rioters or those who were left.
sentences.zh: 所以他们杀死了所有其他暴徒或者说幸存者。

sentences.en: But they're left with a smoking, smouldering capital city, basically.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，留给他们的只是一座冒着烟、余烬未熄的首都。

sentences.en: Shall I read you what John the Lydian said about it?
sentences.zh: 要我读读约翰·利杜斯对此是怎么说的吗？

sentences.en: I'd love to hear what John the Lydian said.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听约翰·利杜斯说了什么。

sentences.en: The city was a series of blackened, blasted hills, like the reaches of a volcano, uninhabitable because of dust, smoke, and the foul stench of building materials reduced to ashes.
sentences.zh: 这座城市是一片焦黑、饱受摧残的山丘，就像火山的边缘，由于尘土、浓烟以及化为灰烬的建筑材料发出的恶臭而无法居住。

sentences.en: And presumably tens of thousands of bodies.
sentences.zh: 想必还有数万具尸体。

sentences.en: 50,000 are called into Procopius.
sentences.zh: 普罗柯比乌斯提到了五万人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if we're saying, you know, the population of Constantinople is half a million, that's a tenth of the city.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们说，你知道的，君士坦丁堡的人口是五十万，那这就是城市十分之一的人口。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not the first time there'll be lots of dead bodies in the streets of Constantinople, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不会是君士坦丁堡街头第一次出现大量尸体。

sentences.en: So a tenth of the population, perhaps, slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许有十分之一的人口被屠杀。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe an exaggeration, probably an exaggeration, but still enormous numbers of casualties.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许有所夸大，可能确实夸大了，但伤亡人数依然极其巨大。

sentences.en: And the whole of central Constantinople wiped out.
sentences.zh: 而且君士坦丁堡的中轴地区全毁了。

sentences.en: But there's good news for Justine in that as well, because there's a lot of good news.
sentences.zh: 但对查士丁尼来说这也是个好消息，因为这里有很多好消息。

sentences.en: He's got rid of a lot of people that he didn't like.
sentences.zh: 他除掉了许多他不喜欢的人。

sentences.en: Plus, he can rebuild the city now as he wants.
sentences.zh: 此外，他现在可以按照自己的意愿重建这座城市。

sentences.en: He can create the imperial city of, you know, you talked about him wanting heaven on earth.
sentences.zh: 他可以创造帝王之城，你知道的，你之前说过他想要人间天堂。

sentences.en: He can create heaven on earth in one building in particular.
sentences.zh: 他可以在某座特定的建筑中创造人间天堂。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Hagia Sophia, the cathedral has burnt down.
sentences.zh: 所以圣索菲亚大教堂被烧毁了。

sentences.en: And the new building, the new Hagia Sophia, starts to rise from the ashes like a phoenix very, very rapidly after the riots,
sentences.zh: 而这座新建筑，也就是新的圣索菲亚大教堂，在暴乱之后非常非常迅速地像凤凰一样从灰烬中崛起，

sentences.en: which suggests that Justine had already been planning it, probably.
sentences.zh: 这表明查士丁尼可能已经提前做好了规划。

sentences.en: So that is one example of the way in which the Nica riots actually end up redounding hugely to his benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是尼卡暴乱最终极大地对他的统治有利的一个例子。

sentences.en: The other, of course, is that, as you said, he's been able to get rid of a lot of his enemies.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个例子是，正如你所说，他得以除掉了许多政敌。

sentences.en: So quite a lot of the senators, they get disinherited, sent into exile.
sentences.zh: 因此，相当多的参议员被剥夺继承权并流放。

sentences.en: Poor Hypatius gets executed.
sentences.zh: 可怜的海帕提乌斯被处决了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He never even wanted to be emperor, the poor fellow.
sentences.zh: 这个可怜的家伙甚至从来没想过当皇帝。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，没有。

sentences.en: Very sad.
sentences.zh: 非常令人难过。

sentences.en: But more importantly, the institutional power of the Senate is now massively, massively diminished.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，参议院的体制权力现在遭到了极大的削弱。

sentences.en: And so everything that Justinian wanted for his role as emperor has basically been consolidated.
sentences.zh: 因此，查士丁尼作为皇帝所期望的一切权力基本上都得到了巩固。

sentences.en: And this is one of the paradoxes of Justinian's reign, is that this man who is ruthlessly, monomaniacly obsessed with restoring the Roman Empire to its former grandeur,
sentences.zh: 这也是查士丁尼统治的悖论之一：这个冷酷无情、有着单一狂热、一心想恢复罗马帝国昔日辉煌的人，

sentences.en: does so much to destroy elements within the new Rome that derive from the old Rome.
sentences.zh: 却做出了那么多摧毁新罗马内部承袭自旧罗马元素的事情。

sentences.en: And so the Nica riots play a key role in the process by which Constantinople becomes that much less Roman,
sentences.zh: 因此，尼卡暴乱在君士坦丁堡变得没那么罗马化的进程中发挥了关键作用，

sentences.en: even as Justinian sees himself legitimately as the kind of archetype of a traditional all-conquering triumphant Caesar.
sentences.zh: 尽管查士丁尼理所当然地把自己视为传统全胜凯撒大帝的某种原型。

sentences.en: And I think that that is the paradox that, in a sense, structures his whole reign.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这个悖论，在某种意义上构成了他整个统治的基础。

sentences.en: It structures the wars that he will very soon be launching westwards to retake Italy and North Africa.
sentences.zh: 它构成了他不久后将向西发起、以夺回意大利和北非的战争的基础。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a note on which we should end this episode.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我们结束本集的一个注脚。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: But just before we do that, Tom, Hagia Sophia.
sentences.zh: 但在我们这样做之前，汤姆，关于圣索菲亚大教堂。

sentences.en: So he builds the new Hagia Sophia.
sentences.zh: 所以他建造了新的圣索菲亚大教堂。

sentences.en: I mean, you must have been to this many times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你一定去过这里很多次。

sentences.en: For me, the building that Justinian – well, it wasn't Justinian, was it?
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这座由查士丁尼建造的建筑——嗯，其实不是查士丁尼，对吧？

sentences.en: It was Anthemius of Trales and Isidore of Miletus.
sentences.zh: 那是特拉勒斯的安提莫斯和米利都的伊西多尔。

sentences.en: With this colossal dome, you can see it right – you can see it to this day in Istanbul.
sentences.zh: 凭借着这个巨大的穹顶，直到今天你都还可以在伊斯坦布尔亲眼看到它。

sentences.en: And to me, there is nothing – I mean, maybe the mosaics of Justinian and Theodore in Ravenna.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，没有什么——我是说，也许拉韦纳的查士丁尼和狄奥多拉的马赛克镶嵌画算吧。

sentences.en: But there is nothing that better captures the grandeur and the might of the Eastern Roman Empire, this empire that Gibbon wrote off as this sort of pitiful relic, corrupt relic.
sentences.zh: 但没有什么能比这更能捕捉到东罗马帝国的宏伟与强盛，这个被吉本贬为可怜残余、腐败残余的帝国。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, to go into the Hagia Sophia, I always find it just the most transcendent experience.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，走进圣索菲亚大教堂，我总是觉得这是一次最超凡脱俗的体验。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the building that more than anything else, I think, serves as the embodiment of Constantinople, of the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 我认为，比起其他任何建筑，它更能体现君士坦丁堡、体现拜占庭帝国的精髓。

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, of course, it stands in a line of descent from the original Rome.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，它当然延续了最初罗马的衣钵。

sentences.en: So the dome is a Roman invention developed from the volcanic ash, actually, that had been spewed up by Vesuvius,
sentences.zh: 所以穹顶是一项罗马发明，实际上是由维苏威火山喷发出的火山灰发展而来的，

sentences.en: developed by Nero, developed famously by Hadrian with the Pantheon in Rome.
sentences.zh: 由尼禄发展，经由哈德良在罗马修建的万神殿发扬光大。

sentences.en: And this vast dome, the largest dome ever built when it was raised, it's the ultimate triumph of Roman engineering.
sentences.zh: 而这个巨大的穹顶，在建造时是史上建造的最大的穹顶，它是罗马工程技术的终极胜利。

sentences.en: But at the same time, of course, it is, unlike the Pantheon, it's built as a church to the glory of God.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，与万神殿不同的是，它是一座为荣耀上帝而建的教堂。

sentences.en: And when Justinian goes in, it is said, he cries out, I have triumphed over you, Solomon.
sentences.zh: 据说当查士丁尼走进去时，他大声喊道：所罗门，我战胜了你。

sentences.en: Solomon, I have surpassed thee.
sentences.zh: 所罗门，我超越了你。

sentences.en: But of course, Solomon, neither Solomon nor Justinian, Tom, had ever recorded a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但当然，汤姆，无论是所罗门还是查士丁尼，都从来没有录过播客。

sentences.en: So they had not yet ascended to the heights of human ingenuity and achievement, as we have.
sentences.zh: 所以他们还没有达到人类才智与成就的高度，就像我们所做的那样。

sentences.en: There's a note on which to end this episode.
sentences.zh: 这就是结束本集的一个注脚。

sentences.en: On that note, on that bombshell, we will reconvene, this was meant to be one episode, by the way, we've just finished episode two.
sentences.zh: 带着这个注脚，带着这个重磅消息，我们将再次聚首——顺便说一句，这本该是一集，我们刚刚完成了第二集。

sentences.en: We will reconvene next time for episode three, where we will be talking about the reign of Justinian and Theodora, Justinian's wars.
sentences.zh: 我们下次将重新聚首开始第三集，我们将讨论查士丁尼和狄奥多拉的统治，以及查士丁尼的战争。

sentences.en: We'll be reflecting on the plague of Justinian, which we touched on last, well, I was going to say last time,
sentences.zh: 我们将反思查士丁尼瘟疫，我们上一次——嗯，我本想说上一次，

sentences.en: but several times ago with Carl Harper, when we talked about disease and the end of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 但其实是好几期之前和卡尔·哈珀一起讨论疾病与罗马帝国终结时的那个话题。

sentences.en: And I suppose Tom will also be talking about Justinian and Theodora's legacy, the way they've been remembered and the way we think about Rome and Byzantium.
sentences.zh: 我想汤姆还会讨论查士丁尼和狄奥多拉的遗产，他们被铭记的方式，以及我们思考罗马和拜占庭的方式。

sentences.en: And we'll be talking about Procopius' secret history, where that is coming from, how accurate, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们还会讨论普罗柯比乌斯的《秘史》，它从何而来，准确度如何，你知道的，

sentences.en: the account of Theodora and the geese and Justinian's face turning into a lumpless, a featureless lump of flesh.
sentences.zh: 关于狄奥多拉和鹅的故事，以及查士丁尼的脸变成了一块没有凸起、没有五官的肉团的说法。

sentences.en: So there's a lot more demons.
